result: ROOT CAUSE of the :app:rustBuildArm64Release failure that had been blocking the Android build. It is a THREE-WAY version split. gen/android/buildSrc/.../BuildTask.kt:27 hardcodes executable="cargo" and runs 'tauri android android-studio-script', so GRADLE USES THE CARGO-INSTALLED tauri-cli, not the npm one. Live versions were: npm @tauri-apps/cli (outer build) 2.11.1 / cargo tauri-cli (invoked by gradle) 2.12.1 / tauri Rust crate 2.11.1. 2.12.1's android-studio-script reads .tauri/cli-options-server.json, a file only 2.12.1's OWN android build writes; the npm 2.11.1 driving the outer build never writes it. Proof the versions were split: strings on the 2.11.1 binary finds 'android-studio-script' but ZERO occurrences of 'cli-options-server', so the error text came from a binary the npm package does not contain. ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-tauri is dated Oct 9 09:54, which is when builds began failing. The error message blames Android Studio, which is a red herring for a CLI build.
method: BuildTask.kt:27 inspection; strings on cli.darwin-arm64.node; cargo tauri --version vs node_modules/.bin/tauri --version
